Ophthalmology · published research

Iridocyclitis

A controlled report described a 40% shorter healing period and faster resolution of inflammatory signs with He-Ne irradiation added to standard therapy. The result is unreplicated and non-randomized.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

A controlled report described a 40% shorter healing period and faster resolution of inflammatory signs with He-Ne irradiation added to standard therapy. The result is unreplicated and non-randomized.

Summary of the Evidence

One human controlled report is listed for iridocyclitis. It includes two groups of 20 eyes and reports He-Ne irradiation as an add-on to standard anti-inflammatory care. No independent clinical replication, animal study, or laboratory report is mapped to this indication. Koev et al. 2010, Acta Medica Bulgarica 37(1):22–29, abstract: Source.

Human and clinical evidence

The report describes patients with acute anterior uveitis or iridocyclitis. Both groups received the same standard anti-inflammatory medicines; the treated group also received daily He-Ne laser irradiation over ten days. The authors report stronger suppression of inflammatory signs, faster disappearance of exudate and keratic precipitates, and a 40% shorter healing period, with p<0.001. Allocation was not randomized, and the report does not provide a modern masked outcome assessment. The effect of laser cannot be separated confidently from other care or study limitations.

Animal evidence

No animal study directly evaluating treatment of iridocyclitis was identified in the mapped category.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No in-vitro or ex-vivo iridocyclitis study was listed.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The abstract specifies 632 nm light at 0.1 mW/cm², applied daily for ten days. It does not fully establish exposure geometry or other dosimetric details. The clinical protocol was combined with medications, and no independent trial has confirmed the schedule.

Interpretation

The observed improvement is a single-study clinical signal, not a replicated estimate. Because all patients received standard treatment and the allocation was non-randomized, the contribution of irradiation remains uncertain. Better controlled studies with prespecified clinical resolution measures are needed.

Evidence strength in source summaryInflammation and time to healing: One small controlled report
Publications and records1 publication: 1 non-randomized controlled human report with 40 eyes in two groups.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

One non-randomized controlled report compared 20 treated eyes with 20 controls, with standard anti-inflammatory treatment in both groups. Faster resolution was reported, but treatment allocation, masking, dosing details, and independent replication are limited. The finding cannot support a broad clinical conclusion.

Publication and study types

  • Both groups received anti-inflammatory treatment, and the intervention group also received He-Ne irradiation.
  • No separate animal or laboratory evidence and no independent clinical cohort are listed.

Research countries listed

  • Bulgaria
